islandAreas.description: How many areas the island has round home, and its round, buffered shape.

island.description: Which island is played: home, built from the kinds she knows, or another by its roster.

found.description: the kinds whose islands she's found (the night's legends favour the others).

phase.description: How an island grows out from home, its outline rounder or more lobed, bayed and armed the further out it is.

coast.description: How irregular the island's coastline is, with gentle bays and headlands rather than a perfect circle.

map.description: The forest's size: how many areas there are and how big each one is.

biomeLooks.description: How strongly an island's forests take on its biome's look, more so the further out its ring.

shore.description: metres of bare shore round the water (no trees, nothing placed).

pad.description: how far from the water anything on foot stops.

koi.description: the share of lakes with koi in them (DECISION FOR ED).

biomeFrom.description: the island phase from which its lakes take the look of its compass biomes on the sea chart (frozen, lava, oasis, sinkhole, glacial tarn, tar pit, rust pool, lily pond; app/chartOutlines.worker.ts), before it plain water.

biomeFirstShare.description: the share of that first phase's lakes that take them, each lake seeded, the rest plain water; further out all of them, further in none.

lakes.description: Lakes on the outer islands: some areas are water she can fly over but not land on, some with biome looks like frozen or lava lakes.

disc.description: its disc drawn in the sky past the rim at its bearing (hidden behind the world).

moon.description: The moon rising and circling over the sea chart each time it opens.

edgeBand.description: (#746: "add empty sea around the edge of the map"): the empty sea past the furthest islands, the disc's radius beyond theirs as a share of it (0 as before; at most 0.6).

sailHold.description: How long the use button is held on an island at the sea chart to sail there.

chart.description: The sea chart (the map table and chart.html; render/chart/seaChart.ts, render/chart/moon.ts).

islands.description: How the other islands look on the sea chart and in the dream bubbles: their coastlines and shapes.

grain.description: how far each of the sand's art pixels is lightened or darkened at random, 0.14 = ±7%; the sand and sea draw their art pixels doubled until each covers at least a screen pixel (render/ground.ts), so the grain stays chunky under the beach's far, low camera.

vary.description: the sand's width round the coast, width times e to the amp times a seeded smooth noise of harmonics bays and narrows; where the noise is lowest (below -rocky, of -1 to 1) it turns rocky, narrowing to rockyWidth metres; never under min.

decor.description: Shells, starfish, seaweed, pebbles and footprint trails scattered along the beach.

dolphins.description: Dolphins leaping off the east coast while she's on the beach.

kraken.description: A kraken's tentacles rising off the west coast now and then while she's on the beach.

beach.description: The strip of sand round the island's edge, where she can lie down to stargaze and meet other witches.

bushes.description: the share of the undergrowth and the ground cover left in its open middle.

arena.description: Every area is kept mostly open round its centre and its soundsystem, so fights have room.

areaSizeVariance.description: How much areas vary in size, some small and some large.

clearingSize.description: (0-1): how far out from an area's centre the ground stays fully open.

clearingFalloff.description: (0-1): over how much of the way to the border trees thicken to full density (small: crisp clearing edges).

gladeAmount.description: How much of the woods is open in random glades.

tufts.description: How far the ground cover blends across area borders as the trees do.

areaEdgeBlend.description: Trees and bushes near an area's border take the look of the area next door, so borders blend rather than form a line.

groundBlend.description: How neighbouring areas' floor textures meet, along a meandering, blended border.

layout.description: Every area's runestone stands on a rise and every legend's clearing lies in a hollow.

ground.description: Low rises and hollows in the ground's lighting, so it doesn't look flat.

wisps.description: Will-o'-the-wisps drifting through the wild areas near her, none near a party.

hue.description: the twilight's colour (a cool violet dusk, against the party's amber).

light.description: its pool, filling the circle and soft at its edge.

edge.description: the ring at its edge at full (a quarter of it always marks the circle), which brightens with the witch inside it or a quest sigil or relic put down in it, easing at edgeEase a second.

motes.description: per to a clearing, rising rise metres a second to height metres, size art pixels, in hue and sat at bright.

glades.description: The clearings where sleeping legends lie.

carrier.description: On other islands, that island's legend carries the treehouse on its back, braced under the oak.

treehouse.description: The witch's home in the great oak beside the dancefloor: where it stands, its deck and rooms, how she walks and lands there, and the oak's crown, lights and warm glow over it.

home.description: Home's area: the map is cut with home first, a circle round the dancefloor out past the treehouse's footprint (its distance and clear) and margin metres more all home's; the areas round it are cut round it, their centres kept at least gap of an area beyond the circle.

featured.description: one of ids (seeded) placed on a map at its chance, in an area it suits if there is room, else in any.

scenes.description: Small vignettes and large landmarks (a farmyard corner, a bus stop, a cemetery, castle ruins) placed about the island.

grounds.description: Old playgrounds and sports grounds in some areas, off to the side of their centre.

minFromStone.description: its edge at least this many metres from its area's runestone (where the soundsystem comes), clear of the stone's clearing and the party's dance space; a small area with no such spot takes the farthest that fits (logged).

minFromOtherStones.description: its edge at least this many metres from every neighbouring area's runestone too, always (not relaxed for a small area).

glint.description: how much the grooves catch the light while its legend sleeps (0, off: Ed's call later).

floor.description: on, old flagstones about slab metres across, the legend's sigil carved into them as dark grooves, overgrowth (0.5 as drawn, up to 1 for more) moss, grass and litter over them so the carving shows only in pieces.

rim.description: art builder 3's rim kit (#262) round its edge, a piece every spacing metres of it at chance, out metres past its radius and up to spread more (on its ring, never its floor), none on a path nor within gap degrees of due south.

grove.description: The forest swells thicker and taller round the edge of a legend's clearing.

fit.description: Each legend's clearing is sized to its legend as drawn asleep, with a margin to spare.

legendClearing.description: Each sleeping legend lies in a small round clearing of its own, sized to fit it.

relics.description: Modern relics (cars, trolleys, cones, highway slabs, a phone box, a sofa) scattered through the forest, more of them near roads.

walls.description: Garden walls, hedges, brambles and rock walls running through the areas, along paths where there are some.

mix.description: each family's share times its factor, 1 as each area authors it.

footprint.description: metres round a decoration kept clear of soundsystems, the dancefloor, the treehouse and set pieces (plus reserveMargin).

decor.description: Ruins, rocks and freak trees scattered as discoveries, fewer under dense canopy.

linkChance.description: the share of neighbouring areas joined by a meandering path.

deadEndChance.description: the share of areas with a path out to nothing.

pathHalf.description: How wide the paths are kept clear of trees, with thick bushes along their edges.

railBroken.description: the share of the railway that's broken, where trees grow between the sleepers (treesOnBroken times the usual chance).

pieces.description: false places none of these 3D pieces at all.

fingerposts.description: a fingerpost by each footpath where it comes into a clearing (the prop generator's; the game turns it on: app/linkParams.ts); the two flights of stairs are finds, each at most once per map, by the clearing of a ravine, rocky slope, cave mouth or stone shrine.

paths.description: Railways, old roads and streams crossing the island.

setPieceChance.description: the share of areas, among the types that have a set piece, that show theirs.

setPieceFootprint.description: Scenery keeps clear of the gameplay places: soundsystems, legends and the like.

treeDensity.description: treeHeight and crownWidth scale the art's trees (1 is the Art Lab's size; crowns widen with treeHeight too, crownWidth is the total).

autumn.description: each tree's lit leaf colour drifts toward its own autumn colour (gold, orange, red, crimson or purple, by its first seed) by up to autumn of the way (its own share of it, some trees barely at all), kept at the brightness the night's moonlight gave it, so a red tree is as dark as its neighbours.

value.description: its leaves' brightness scaled by 1 + value times the second seed (on the pixels its sway mask marks as leaves: the wood is untouched; both halves alike).

hue.description: Each tree's leaf colour turned a little either way, so neighbouring trees don't look identical.

leafJitter.description: Each tree's own leaf colour: every tree is dealt two fixed seeds from where it stands (-1 to 1 each).

treetop.description: the share of it seen over the treetops (gentler).

wind.description: Wind sway on leafy things (Ed, v171): trees (both halves together, from the foot) and undergrowth lean with gusts that travel across the forest: strength metres at the top of a crown, gusts moving at speed m/s, gustScale metres across; Walls and set pieces stand still.

groundCover.description: Tufts of grass, fern, heather, reeds, moss and clover on the ground round her, so the ground doesn't look flat.

density.description: How thick the trees grow: dense patches, sparse patches and glades rather than an even forest.

treeCap.description: How tall the tallest trees (tall and giant) are drawn.

pins.description: The HUD's pointers as map pins over their subject (render/indicator.ts): gap is how far (screen pixels) the arrow's tip floats over the subject's drawn top.

canopyReach.description: in the treetops, tree crowns alone (no trunk, shadow or undergrowth) are drawn out to this many metres (at most haze.far) where the budget has pulled the rest in closer, so the canopy stays whole to the horizon on a slow machine; 0 off.

scenery.description: How far round her trees, bushes and other scenery are drawn; creatures and gameplay objects are always drawn.

acceleration.description: how quickly she reaches her speed or stops in the treetops (per second; higher is snappier).

cameraPull.description: how far the camera draws back at full boost (a share of its distance).

treetop.description: Treetop flight: a high top speed with momentum, building a boost while she holds a direction.

leanAt.description: the share of the top speed above which she leans into her flight.

facing.description: When she and the creatures turn away from the viewer, only when clearly heading up the screen.

riseCooldown.description: After she lands she can't rise again for this many seconds.

cooldown.description: One shared cooldown for her dodge and her take-off.

knock.description: A blow knocks her back and staggers her, harder for big attacks and charges.

witch.description: Her speeds on the ground and in the treetops, how long rising and descending take, and how the world's lights light her.

stack.description: The stack of sigils above her hat, swaying like a chain of springs as she moves.

grace.description: seconds after a hit in which no other blow lands, so a pack striking together takes one hit, not all three.

slashScale.description: her claw slashes' size relative to her.

slashGlow.description: their glow, the berries' light drawn in the scene along each stroke so the bloom takes it.

witchHealth.description: The witch: she takes hits (one point each, whatever hits her) before she's knocked out; one comes back every repairTime seconds, the timer starting over whenever she's hit, so to heal she has to get right out of the fight.

legendsLoyal.description: leashed legends stay with her (false: they're let go too: 'they're too old for this'; only a party legend is ever leashed now, and it's always let go).

dropHat.description: When knocked out she drops her hat where she fell, and wears none till she goes back and picks it up.

dim.description: how much the screen dims round her while her hat floats off, from the knockdown to her sparkle away (her spot and the hat left lit); no hat, no dim.

rise.description: the house (rules/treehouse.ts): back at the magic circle after a knockout, she rises out of its floor over rise seconds, then walks to her decks and scratches for the rest of the wait.

candleStep.description: one candle for every candleStep seconds of the wait (1 or 0.5), white for the base wait, red for the extra from knockdowns in a row; the red burn first.

knockout.description: What happens when she's knocked out: her creatures go free, she comes back at the treehouse after a wait that grows with each knockdown, and the beat speeds up.

buffer.description: a press up to this many seconds before she can blink (still recharging, landing, staggered) waits and blinks the moment she can.

chain.description: the least time, seconds, from one blink to the next, whatever her charges or the shared cooldown say (it keeps a Double blink's two apart; the legend buffs' blink chain, 0.2, before they were removed).

toCursor.description: on, she blinks toward the ground under the cursor (or the way the right stick points), the way she faces when the cursor is within aimDead metres of her, and with nothing to aim by (touch) the way she's steering; off, always the way she's steering.

dash.description: The dash: on the ground she blinks a short way in the direction she's moving and can't be hit for a moment.

hats.description: the spell hats she owns, a comma list or * for every one.

parts.description: her broom's parts, a comma list of ids from config/broom-parts.json (the page sets it from her save, localStorage witch.broom, fitted at the Workshop's bay; ?parts= for one load); the bare broom, none, has no spell and no quick take-off, and a complete set gives its spell.

speed.description: the Speed broom, her speed times mult for duration seconds, then cooldown seconds to recharge.

healing.description: The Healing ring heals her while she stands near it, and the Helmet takes the first blow for her.

battering.description: the Battering broom's blink stuns every wild and enraged creature within width m of its line for stun s.

leyjump.description: the Ley jump broom, cast, puts her at the ley line's pulse; cooldown s.

pound.description: the Ground pound broom, cast, rises or lands at once, knocking wild and enraged creatures within radius m back push m, and landing stuns them stun s; cooldown s.

stealth.description: the Stealth broom: creatures don't see her unless she threw a 💌 or put down or picked up something in the last reveal s; ones that went for her keep on while she's within range m, then lose her.

harvest.description: the Harvest hat, put down, grows berries berries in a ring radius m round it, at most once every every s (the same ring, moved: uneaten ones move with it).

dowsing.description: the Dowsing hat, put down, points to the nearest relic for time s.

sentry.description: the Sentry hat, lying there, throws a 💌 at the nearest invitable creature within range m every every s (Ed: larger ranges).

slingshot.description: the Slingshot hat catches her 💌s flying within catch m, circling it radius m out, holds them hold s and flings each at the nearest invitable creature within fire m, at most max at once.

gathering.description: the Gathering hat, picked up again, brings every sigil of hers within range m back to her stack (Ed: all sigils in range).

bramble.description: the Bramble hat slows wild and enraged creatures within range m of it (Ed: 30 m).

mine.description: the Mine hat, put down, stuns wild and enraged creatures within range m for stun s, at most once every every s.

lullaby.description: the Lullaby hat, put down, sends wild creatures (not enraged) within range m to sleep for time s, at most once every every s; one wakes when a 💌 lands on it.

cyclone.description: The Cyclone hat sweeps nearby wild and enraged creatures round it, lifts them and flings them away.

nursing.description: the Nursing hat heals her own creatures within range m of it, rate of their health a second (0.1: whole again in ten seconds).

spells.description: Her two spell slots, a hat and a broom, each holding a spell or none.

width.description: metres across on the ground and over the treetops.

fade.description: how it fades along its length (eased out: bright for its first stretch, then thinning to nothing; higher keeps it bright longer), its width tapering with it.

sparks.description: the broom's little amber sparks as well.

trail.description: Her flight trail: a glowing ribbon along her path in the colour of the area she's over.

swoopTrail.description: Rainbow trails the party witches leave as they swoop.

glow.description: How strongly a berry's soft halo glows.

berries.description: Berries on the bushes of every area, which her creatures eat to evolve.

arc.description: the height (m) its lob rises over the straight line from her hand to the ground at its range, where it lands, with a puff (drawn only: the rules fly it flat).

hits.description: How many letters it takes to win a creature over by its level, and how fast its meter drains when not being hit.

fireSlow.description: her ground speed while firing, times this.

linger.description: a 💌 that met no one rests where it came down this many seconds, fading over the last lingerFade, at most lingerMax at once (drawn only: it's no hit).

spin.description: How fast a 💌 spins in flight.

orbit.description: the 💌 ring circles a creature at scale times its body radius (movement.json bodies) plus gap metres, at least min, and wider still when it holds many.

hard.description: the hard homing of the 💌s her Sentry and Slingshot hats throw: homing degrees a second, cone degrees either side it looks in, range metres it looks out to (was the legend buffs' charm, 420, 80 and 18).

invites.description: The 💌 invite: on the ground she fires spinning love letters at creatures to win them over.

invite.description: The old proximity chat, now replaced by the 💌 invite: she talked with the nearest creature in emoji.

win.description: The end of the route: after the last wave a pointer leads her to the remaining enraged creatures, then the victory lap.

length.description: how far a leashed creature roams from its leash point (you, or its sigil on the ground).

runSpeed.description: how fast it hurries back when out of range (m/s).

pickRadius.description: how near a placed sigil you must be to pick it up.

spacing.description: how close two sigils may be put down (keep it above pickRadius, or a blocked spot picks up instead of fizzling).

runeRadius.description: how near (m) she picks up a happy creature's rune, a relic's sigil or her hat.

hatHold.description: seconds she holds the sigil button on the ground, with nothing it picks up or puts down, to put her hat down at her feet (just a marker; a press over it puts it back on; rules/hat.ts putHat).

placedThrough.description: how bright a placed sigil shows where grass, bushes, trees or other scenery hide it (0 hidden, 1 as bright as in the open); never through the witch.

sigilGlyph.description: How bright sigil glyphs are drawn, so they don't bloom into blobs on lit ground.

sigilBacking.description: A dark patch under every sigil on the ground, so it reads clearly.

runeGap.description: a happy creature's rune lies south of it (down the screen), and a parked animal roams round a point the same way north of its sigil, by its size: its body radius, half the sigil with its backing, and runeGap metres between (rules/runeOffset.ts; it was a fixed restAbove, 5 m).

hex.description: Sigils are put down and picked up on a fixed hex grid on the ground, so a cluster of them reads cleanly.

runs.description: Holding the sigil button picks up, or puts down, sigils one after another as she runs.

runePull.description: on the ground, the nearest happy creature with its rune within radius (m) trots toward her at speed (m/s), stopping stop (m) from her, so its rune comes to her.

grounded.description: Too many heavy creatures on her leash stop her taking off.

drag.description: moving away from the pull, that part of her speed is divided by 1 + drag x load (her input still steers).

drift.description: she drifts toward the pull at up to that share of her top speed, reached at an extreme load.

rise.description: rising takes 1 + rise x load times as long.

sink.description: Heavily loaded over the treetops she sinks toward the crowns, and lands if she stops.

babyGround.description: a baby's weight on the ground (the treetops' is weight.levels), so 8 fill either allowance; a baby's species strength doesn't count, and in the line its leash's tension is measured from its place in the line.

weight.description: How the creatures on her leash pull on her: slower moving away from them, slower to rise, and sinking in the treetops when heavily loaded.

babies.description: Her leashed babies follow her in single file and scatter out of the way while she's in a fight.

ranks.description: Leash sigils drawn as bare glyphs in their rank's colour (baby, youth, adult, legend) with embers rising off them, so ranks are easy to tell apart at a glance.

bond.description: How a leashed creature shows its tie to its sigil: a glow at its feet, sparks, and a thread when the leash is strained.

scale.description: every length in a fight times this (attack ranges, lunges, area radii, beam widths, knockback, the packs' patterns and spacing, pursuit and guard reach, aggro).

speed.description: every fight speed times this (running, charging, lunging, shots).

momentum.description: How heavily creatures in a fight speed up, brake and turn.

contact.description: it hurts every foe it touches on the way, once each (her grace making one charge one hit).

miss.description: a charge that struck nothing stands winded that many seconds after (stars round its head), an opening for her 💌s.

charge.description: every species' charge (movement.json) scaled: reach its run's time and overshoot past its target, turn its turn rate (lower: wider arcs), brake how hard it slows (lower: more momentum).

fight.description: The scale and speed fights are played at, with creatures running at about her speed.

turn.description: its heading swings at most turn / (1 + its speed / k) degrees a second (also divided by fight.momentum), slowing to turn tighter when she's far off its heading, so a fast one sidestepped overshoots in an arc.

delay.description: it steers for where she was that many seconds ago (a short trail of her places), so a sidestep or blink fools it a moment.

chaseLead.description: seconds of her velocity it leads her by when just chasing (0: none).

strikeLead.description: times the lead its telegraphed attacks take (a melee wind-up's tracking, dodge.a.lead; a charge's lane, dodge.b.chargeLead; a leap, fight.leap.lead; a swoop's dive; shots and lobs, dodge.b.lead).

classes.description: each class's values (heavy: dodge.a.heavy's species; light: those with the nimble or swarm trait; normal: everyone else), and a species may set its own in its folder (art/creatures/<id>/creature.js movement.momentum).

creatureMomentum.description: Creatures chasing her carry momentum on their run-in and wind-up, so she can dodge past them.

legendFlash.description: how much bigger and longer a legend's blow flashes than anyone's (its flash 1 + 2 × legendFlash times; 0.5, twice: Ed's decisions panel, config/decisions.json).

attackFx.description: How attacks feel on screen: attackers crouch and lunge, hits squash their target, and hard knock-backs send it tumbling.

packs.description: Pack kinds fight in combos (the nearest lunges, the ranged fire where she'd dodge, one behind her throws its special) and fall back between them.

aggro.description: wild creatures go for party animals within this, and for the witch anywhere in their area.

leaveArea.description: How far past its area's edge a wild creature chases her before giving up and going home.

pursuit.description: how far from her (or its sigil, guarding) a party animal chases a foe before giving up.

pursuitRun.description: how fast it closes in while over 30 m off (so an area's creatures are onto her in a few seconds when she lands in it).

fightRun.description: how fast a creature runs in a fight (m/s), when its movement profile doesn't say (movement.json speed).

reaction.description: seconds before a creature that has just noticed something goes for it.

shake.description: how hard a legend's quake shakes the screen (0 none).

daze.description: seconds a wild creature knocked down in a fight lies stunned (nothing attacks it, it attacks nothing, she can still invite it; it counts as present for its legend, and no siege takes it) before it runs off home.

defendRadius.description: her animals following her within this many metres of her go first for anything attacking her, spread over her attackers; farther off, following her, one fights back only at what's on it itself (and parked, guarding or travelling ones carry on as they were): never pulled across to her fight.

taunt.description: a creature after her that one of her animals in her fight hits turns on that animal instead, with chance chance, for time seconds (a lunge at her already under way lands first; then it may come back to her).

combat.description: How creatures fight: who goes for whom, how fast they run and chase, and how much a soundsystem and home's speakers can take.

notice.description: Creatures notice her on the ground nearby: resting ones turn to look, curious babies come up to her.

heavy.description: Heavy kinds chasing her build up speed and swing their charges toward her, so a burst or a blink gets clear.

dodge.description: Dodging matters: creatures commit to their strikes, so she can dodge them by moving or blinking away.

on.description: false lets them roam the whole area as before.

stoneIdle.description: A wild area's hostile creatures gather and roam near its runestone.

on.description: false lets them stand on sigils as before.

pad.description: Metres past a sigil's edge a creature's middle still counts as on it.

sigilAvoid.description: Idling and dancing creatures keep off the sigils lying on the floor.

on.description: false: they attack at once, as before.

inviteWakes.description: a 💌 landing on one of a wild area's creatures wakes the area at once: its watch is over (or never starts), and its own young and adults, napping or not, wake with no getting up and go for her at once, by the hunt's rules (rules/inviteWakes.ts); its babies, legend and circle baby as before.

wildWatch.description: On her first landing in a wild area its creatures stare and redden for a few seconds before they attack, and how far they chase her after.

on.description: false: the old rule (only those near her attack).

hunt.description: Once the wild watch is over, every awake young and adult in the area hunts her while she's in it.

circle.description: a legend circle's baby naps at each pause with its own chance, for its own length (seconds), and is woken only by a witch on the ground within reach metres of its circle's edge (so she can still invite it), not anywhere in its area.

naps.description: Wild creatures roaming their area now and then lie down for a nap.

guard.description: Creatures parked at a sigil on the ground guard it, fighting any wild creature that comes near.

babies.description: babies in every area, start's included, at most babyCap.

minHostile.description: at least this many young or adults in every wild area, any shortfall made up with young.

classes.description: Swarm species come in strong, medium and light classes, smaller swarms of stronger creatures.

population.description: How many wild creatures each area starts with, more along the waves' route so the later areas are the dangerous ones.

simLod.description: How far from her wild creatures are simulated every step; further off they're simulated coarsely, and past the sim radius not at all.

creatureSpeeds.description: The witch is much faster than almost all creatures.

legendCircle.description: Standing in a sleeping or restless legend's circle slows the whole world down.

nightmare.description: a restless legend's one face, slightly sad to angry: faces[k] from restlessness at[k] on.

sleepy.description: A sleeping legend's sleepy face beside its quest sigil, now and then another face.

cycle.description: the pixel thought bubble shows one symbol for hold seconds, the face, then the sigil it dreams of, then the face again; a flask share of the sigil's turns (seeded per legend and turn) show the flask's relic sigil instead; each fades in and out over fade seconds.

dreams.description: A sleeping legend's dream bubble, showing the quest it wants, and a pointer to where to go.

earlyQuest.description: One of the first areas the waves wake has a legend dreaming of a creature from a nearby area, so there's an early quest.

areas.description: Each legend gets an area of its own beside one of its kind's areas.

questLater.description: a legend dreams only of a kind living in an area later on the route than its own, within questCap areas; failing that, the kind of the nearest later area; with no later area, any kind (the early easy quest keeps its own pick); false: any kind as before.

bombard.description: ("Legend bombards, but prioritises you"): an angry legend with no witch in its reach throws the first lob or beam of its volley at the nearest standing soundsystem within range metres, damage a hit (of combat.soundsystemHealth); a charging legend lobs at it rather than charge.

stomp.description: A legend turning angry destroys its own area's soundsystem at once.

legends.description: Which areas have a legend, and how far a happy one reaches.

dark.description: a legend whose floored look (seen.floor times its coat's luminance, its body colour as baked: render/legendLight.ts) is under seen.dark has its floor raised to seen.dark over that luminance, at most seen.liftMax; the bear, the boar and the others as dark are caught, lighter legends stay as they are.

wildLegends.description: What legends are for: optional quests, relics for powerful allies, and danger to her babies in sieges.

beat.description: The party's tempo in beats per minute, which the lasers sweep to and party animals dance to.

pulseSpeed.description: How fast the pulse runs along the ley line, which sets how long each wave takes to arrive.

reveal.description: How fast the ley line grows out from the treehouse ahead of the waves, so no stone pops on at once.

advance.description: Whether the ley line moves on to the next stone only when its wave arrives, or as soon as that area's quest is done.

brightness.description: How bright the ley line glows, each stretch shading from one area's colour to the next.

depart.description: How the first stretch of ley line leaves the treehouse, curving round the ring of speakers rather than crossing the dancefloor.

leyLines.description: The glowing line on the ground that joins the runestones in the order the waves wake them, a pulse flowing along it to the next one.

exclude.description: pieces never placed, loose or in clusters.

generated.description: the prop generator's seeded bunting, balloon bunches and paper lanterns (art/party.js gen-*) in place of the hand-made ones they replace (the game turns it on: app/viewParams.ts).

partyObjects.description: The party clutter that appears as an area is partified: litter, lights, balloons, lanterns in the trees and set dressing, and home's own.

gaze.description: Beds out past the speakers where party witches lie stargazing, which she can join.

partyWitches.description: Other witches who fly in to dance, drink, chat and swoop around the dancefloor, one per playing soundsystem.

speakerLasers.description: A single laser beam swinging up from each speaker in the dancefloor's ring.

lasers.description: Each playing soundsystem's laser show, its beams fanning and sweeping in time with the music.

twinkle.description: How the sparks along a partified area's border twinkle, flicker and swap colours with the area next door.

borders.description: A sparkling line round the partified region's outside edge, in each area's sigil colour: width (px), brightness, sparkle (0-1, how much it twinkles and runs), step (metres between its sparks).

levelScale.description: a creature's bubble, emoji and outline together, times this by its level (baby, young, adult, legend); the witch's stays at 1.

bubbles.description: The speech and thought bubbles: outline only, with pixel emoji, sized by the speaker's level.

variants.description: Each area's rune stone is one of twenty carved forms, all used before any repeats.

lightRange.description: stones within this many metres light the scene.

runeMarkers.description: The rune stones marking where soundsystems will come, glowing, and pulsing on the beat when the next wave is coming to them.

voices.description: the most one-shot sounds at once (0: no limit); over it, those that matter least (far creatures, the beds' scattered details) aren't played and lesser ones playing are cut short for her own sounds and the stings.

witch.description: each 💌 a syllable in her voice (pitch Hz, range: how far her phrases rise and fall, pace: a syllable's seconds, timbre: her formants over an adult's, phraseGap: a pause this long starts a new phrase).

animals.description: Creatures babble in their own voice when they attack, a few at a time.

hit.description: a 💌 landing (a spent one a faint tick).

fill.description: the affection tick, climbing octaves as the meter fills.

enraged.description: the growl when one turns (gap: at most one every gap seconds, a crowd turning at once one heavier growl).

snore.description: a sleeping legend within range metres moaning softly in its dreams (volume).

windup.description: a legend's attack winding up, its whale song swelling for length seconds before it fires.

lost.description: a soundsystem lost, the sting heard anywhere (volume).

ouch.description: the witch hurt, her cry and a thump (volume; knocked down, her "whoa-oh" at knockdown times that), the music dipped by duck for duckTime seconds (twice that knocked down).

impact.description: a lobbed shot landing, a thud (small times volume) or a legend's boom (volume), heard from the lob's landing spot (a legend's twice as far).

roar.description: a legend turning angry, its roar (heard twice as far).

power.description: The crackle, whine and thump of a runestone turning into a speaker or soundsystem, each a step up the scale.

lament.description: A restless legend's sad call, heard from the way of its clearing, more often as its restlessness runs out.

shoes.description: dancers within range metres tapping their party shoes on the beat, at most max at once.

pond.description: by a pond within range metres, water lapping (lap), a frog every frogEvery seconds or so (frogs), a drip every dripEvery (drips).

picnic.description: by a picnic in a partified area within range metres, its party-goers' murmur and cups clinking every clinkEvery seconds or so.

aggro.description: The wild watch's warning sound: a low swell and a riser while creatures stare at her, and a hit as they attack.

sparkler.description: by the ley line's pulse, its tip a burning sparkler (art builder 2's #491), its fizz within range metres (louder as she nears it): a flickering hiss (hiss) and a crackle of pops (pops), rate sparks a second, a share fork of them forking into a double tick, times volume.

fireworks.description: The fireworks' whoosh, boom and crackle, and the crowd's cheer at the finale.

seaLife.description: what lives in the sea off the beach, heard within range metres of it, under the music and the waves: a dolphin leaping off the east coast (splash: its blow and its splash back in), the kraken off the west coast (groan: a deep distant moan.

room.description: the creator's room in the treehouse while it's open, its hum, a record's crackle, the timber creaking every creakEvery seconds or so, and after the spell, at her decks before the first home speaker, at decks times its level.

deck.description: The sounds of her decks while she DJs: record scratches, her "woo-hoo!" and the needle dropping.

land.description: a 💌 that met no one landing on the ground, a soft puff (at most one every gap seconds).

nope.description: a soft two-note "uh-uh" at volume, at most one each gap seconds.

alarm.description: her phone ringing in the dark, a run of six bright plucks at volume, rung again every gap seconds while it rings.

cleared.description: a small "cleared!" sting on the next half-beat, at volume, from the new soundsystem, fading over range metres to no less than floor of itself (she cleared it: she hears it).

tempoUp.description: the crowd cheering on the beat the party starts speeding up, at volume (a share of the fireworks' cheer; 0 off).

stir.description: the boot-up over, the first wave's countdown begun, things stirring (volume).

knock.description: the witch knocked back (#108), a thump and a whoosh by how far (volume, whoosh), and stunned, a soft dizzy twinkle every twinkleEvery seconds (twinkle).

charge.description: a legend's long charge, its windup's bellow, heavy hoofbeats by its speed, the ground's rumble along its lane, the skid of its braking arc, a lighter trot home, heard within range metres.

relic.description: a relic bottle found (a rare chime), spotted within spot metres on the ground or spotTreetop from the treetops, or reached within reach.

meadow.description: Home's ambience: breeze, bees, birdsong, a picnic's murmur, clinking cups and squeaking balloons.

whale.description: the legends' voice: volume, speed (1: moans of 2 to 3 s; 2: twice as fast), depth (Hz of its lowest moan), reverb (how big its space), sleepEvery (seconds between a sleeper's moans, sooner when restless).

sail.description: sailing between islands in place (app/sail.ts), the sea's hush and waves (sea, a share) and a soft gusting wind (wind) at volume while the next island is made, fading in and out over about fade seconds, the old night's music fading out over fade seconds as it comes in.

ambience.description: each area's own soundscape in play, the afterparty night's layers without their pad and bells (bed 0), its noise and sounds at noise and sounds, times volume; near the party it keeps only quiet of itself, by how loud the music is there, and gives way to the night once the party's over.

sadTrumpet.description: The sad trumpet when she's knocked down, and the backwards record scratch as she's whisked back to her decks.

sfx.description: The sound effects, all synthesised in the music's key: volume over the music's, hear metres (a sound fades to nothing that far from her).

latency.description: the audio context's latencyHint: interactive the smallest output buffer, balanced more room for the audio thread, playback the most (under-runs least likely, sound effects latest); ?latency= tries one for a load (DECISION FOR ED).

buffer.description: How much audio the game buffers ahead, so the music stays on the beat without crackling.

dropLayers.description: when her needle-drop routine ends after the party spell, that many of the intro's layers come in on the next bar line, each home speaker then adding its own on top.

radius.description: the clearing's metres round a legend where the map draws none.

circle.description: in a sleeping legend's clearing on the ground, the music muffled to muffle Hz and quiet times its volume, eased in and out with a time constant of ease seconds, and the legend's own layer (the music style's circle) over it at level.

muffle.description: on the house its low-pass closes to this many Hz as its world slows (eased with the slowing), its volume as it is; lighter than a legend circle's circle.muffle.

src.description: an audio file to loop (empty: the built-in loop at beat.bpm until there's a real track).

music.description: The music gets louder and clearer near a playing soundsystem and quieter and muffled far off, never silent.

linger.description: seconds it stays after the last blow.

fall.description: seconds a fallen one stays, flashing then fading.

most.description: how many show at once (the most recently hit).

alarms.description: The soundsystem alarm: a soundsystem (or the home ring's speakers) hit while off screen shows a 🔇 at the screen's edge toward it, its ring its health, shaking at each blow.

transform.description: the seconds each takes to turn, glowing and rising into the speaker.

boot.description: At the start the home ring of speakers boots up one stone at a time before the first wave sets off.

motes.description: sparse glowing motes over every partified area, perPatch per 20 x 20 m, rising from from to to metres (under the crowns to above them) at about speed m/s.

uplight.description: Tree crowns in partified areas catch a faint glow from below in the area's colour, pulsing on the beat.

picker.description: how the next area to wake is chosen: route wakes them in one order worked out per map so the ley line through them all crosses itself at most a few times, within Ed's rules: a spiral.

noisy.description: (the picker before it, and the route's own fallback past the crossing rules) chooses among the areas bordering the party as below.

transition.description: seconds an area takes to partify, 0 to skip the show.

style.description: prints (footprints at its stride, left and right; four-legged ones in pairs, insects a tiny track; flyers, birds and snakes drip drops instead), prints+drops (and drops when badly hurt) or drops (drops only).

colour.description: red (a dark red on the night palette) or neon (a deep shade of the creature's own neon).

rate.description: drops a second at none of its health left (by how hurt, squared).

cap.description: The most blood marks shown at once, the oldest giving way.

blood.description: Blood trails: a hurt creature within range metres of her leaves small dark-red pixel marks on the ground as it moves, fading over fade seconds; the more hurt, the more often and the redder.

soundsystemGen.description: Each area's soundsystem is generated with its own look, bigger and taller the further from the dancefloor.

more.description: times as many runs an area, their spread apart shrunk by its square root to fit (1 as tuned).

stringLights.description: Colourful garlands of string lights strung tree to tree across every partified area.

size.description: a digit's height as a share of the screen's.

lift.description: metres above the stone (or the treetops).

spent.description: how bright the number stays once the party has reached the area (0 hides it).

waveNumbers.description: Numbers over the rune stones showing which wave will wake each one (now switched off).

tiles.description: The dancefloor's glass tiles light up under her and on events, show the island's sigil during the boot, and glow brighter as more areas join the party.

dancefloor.description: The dancefloor at the island's heart: its size, its ring of stone speakers, the clearing round it and the magic motes rising off it.

ease.description: seconds it eases in over (g.partyOver.ease, 0 to 1: the lights going out, the music winding down, the ley line fading to leyFloor of its brightness).

walk.description: their pace home, times their roaming speed (they walk, not run: a stroll home after the party).

partyOver.description: The party's over: once the home ring's speakers are all down, the afterparty, any soundsystem still standing switched off: the waves stop, nothing fights, and every creature walks home and sleeps.

sail.description: Sailing from the sea chart starts the next night on the same page, the old night's music fading into sea and wind, rather than reloading.

loading.description: The loading screen: the World Tree and COVEN RUSH picked out in gold stars that light up as the game loads.

wake.description: the wake-up in her bedroom (rules/wakeUp.ts): snooze, a snooze's seconds (Ed: 5, as often as she likes); stretch, her stretch's seconds before she stands; alarmMin, the seconds the alarm rings before E can snooze it.

opening.description: A plain first load wakes her in her bedroom on the home island while the night is made.

handoff.description: where the chart hands over, sea metres out to sea off the south coast below the dancefloor (negative: inland), its camera dist metres back and pitchDeg degrees down (the first flight's: -40, 600, 50); ?dive=near|far|skim for one load (app/chartView.ts DIVES).

tree.description: Where the camera ends its arrival: the whole treehouse tree seen from the south, filling the frame.

arrive.description: Arriving on an island from the sea chart: the camera flies in over the sea, frames the dancefloor and comes round to the treehouse.

zoomEase.description: How softly zooming and rising change the camera's angle and distance.

beyond.description: how many metres past the bent ground's horizon the distant treetops are still drawn (fewer is cheaper).

curve.description: the world bends away toward the top of the screen, per metre ahead of the witch, eased in as she rises; ?curve=<treetop> tries values (0.0015: about 11% of the screen sky in ?bare=1, Ed v276 asked 10-12%; 0.0022 about 24%; under 0.001 none; 0 off).

speedZoom.description: the treetop camera's distance is times (treetopSpeed / base) to the power power, so at a faster treetopSpeed it zooms out and the screen holds about as many seconds of flight (power 0: off).

shake.description: The screen shakes when she's hit, harder for each hit she was already missing and hardest on a knockdown.

circle.description: In a legend's circle the camera tilts and frames her and the legend together.

house.description: landed on the treehouse's floor, the camera eases over ease seconds to angle degrees and its distance times distance.

aim.description: with no part, the camera aimed that share of her height (as she's drawn) up her.

parts.description: Where the camera aims at a dressing station for each part of her being changed (head, hat, top, legs, feet, broom, the pegboard).

station.description: at a dressing station and choosing (the pointer or the d-pad in its panel, or stood still a moment: ui/stationPanel.ts), its distance times distance and moved side times that distance east (west when negative), so she stands clear of the panel; eased over ease seconds, and back as soon as she moves.

camera.description: The camera: near-isometric on the ground, starting close in on her seat in the treehouse and easing out once she moves.

pixelSize.description: How many screen pixels each art pixel takes up, the size of the game's chunky pixels.

spriteTilt.description: 1 = sprites face the camera fully, 0 = stand upright.

creatures.description: From the treetops each leashed or happy creature's sigil hangs over it, moving with it.

sigilProjection.description: From the treetops each placed sigil shows above the canopy over its spot, with a faint beam down to it.

seeThrough.description: tall things in front of her fading (occlusion).

holeCut.description: the canopy cut away round her (off: crowns everywhere).

trunkFade.description: trunk tops fading where crowns are cut away.

groundCover.description: the tufts kept to the cut-away's reach (off: out to groundCover.radius).

glow.description: her light and its warm pool.

effectsLayer.description: the smooth effects layer (mist, dapple: drawn at the scene's resolution and blurred, laid over the picture).

areaAverage.description: scenery sprites averaged where they shrink.

cutWhole.description: the cut-away by each crown whole, as canopyCutout.whole has it (off: pixel by pixel).

seeSplit.description: the see-through's fade itself (off: the soft circle's things stay solid and in the solid pass; the vertex side unchanged).

seeMark.description: the pixels the see-through pass draws tinted magenta.

mist.description: the low mist (in the effects layer).

lightRings.description: the moonlight rings on the crowns (in the effects layer).

seeWrite.description: the see-through pass writes its depth as it draws, so the nearer of two faded things wins where they overlap, as in the solid pass (off as ever: whichever is drawn last).

seeCull.description: the see-through pass skipping, before drawing, every sprite it reckons can't reach her circle or the hole (off: it draws them all and lets each pixel decide).

seeKeep.description: the solid pass keeps what's in front of her as well (the see-through pass drawn over it).

seeStencil.description: the see-through pass marks scenery in the stencil as the solid pass does.

seeEarly.description: the see-through pass drawn straight after the solid scenery (render order 0.6, not 11: she then shows through it whole).

seeSolid.description: the see-through pass's pixels drawn at alpha 1: off, all, only those in her circle (circle) or only the rest (rest).

seeNoBlend.description: the see-through pass drawn with no blending.

seeShowAlpha.description: the see-through pass drawn as its own opacity in grey (white solid, black clear).

showBroken.description: scene pixels that are not a number red, infinite magenta, negative yellow (before the post-process).

seeDither.description: the see-through done in the solid pass as an ordered dither (no second pass for it).

seeTwo.description: the fix (on): what's in front of her drawn in a see-through pass of its own, writing depth, before the half-faded things (off: one see-through pass, as before, the circle bug).

suspects.description: The circle-bug suspects: each effect centred on her with a round edge, on (as ever) or off, read every frame so the pause page's toggles show at once.

occlusion.description: Tall things standing in front of the witch fade where they cover her, so she's never lost from view.

edge.description: (a share of the screen's width) and depth (metres) are how far past its box on screen and nearer than its centre each thing eases from gone to whole, so nothing snaps at a line.

legend.description: a legend's circle (its own radius, its ring pad metres wider for the rim's stones, and its legend as drawn, asleep or awake).

bounded.description: (the runestone's): only what stands within radius metres of the thing fades, so the woods round a fight don't thin out past it.

runestone.description: an area's runestone and its fight's open middle.

find.description: tonight's trunk or wreck, until it's taken.

flask.description: Whether a lying relic flask is kept clear like the other places of interest.

reveal.description: Places of interest she stands in are kept clear: whatever stands in front of them and covers them fades away.

canopyShadow.description: a dappled shadow from the canopy overhead (height in metres), thinner in clearings, drifting with the wind.

rig.description: Creatures close to the camera on the ground are drawn with a live rig (moving limbs) rather than baked frames; legends always are.

pathFade.description: Every end of a path, road, railway or stream (where it stops, peters out or is broken) frays out over its last metres in an ordered dither on the art's pixel grid, broken up by noise (Ed, v149).

trunkFade.description: On the ground, where the crowns are hidden, each trunk's top fades out in a pixel dither instead of ending in a flat cut.

load.description: The weight of her leashed creatures made visible: her sigil stack sags and leans toward the pull, and she leans and her broom bows as she flies away from it.

whole.description: How much the canopy hole fades each crown as a whole rather than pixel by pixel, so the crowns don't line up into rings.

ragged.description: its outline's bays and points round her, a share of the radius, drifting slowly round.

spread.description: each tree's own radius spread round the hole's, a share of it (0.2 before), so the edge is several crowns deep and ragged.

lead.description: its middle leans that many seconds ahead of her the way she's going (eased), so the opening opens into her path.

hold.description: the share of the camera's way down (by its eased lift, which trails hers) the hole stays shut before it opens from nothing, its soft edge growing with it, and so the share of its way up by which it has shut

canopyCutout.description: On the ground the forest roof stays drawn at the screen's edges, with a hole cut round her so she can be seen.

find.description: Wild creatures are easier to find in the dark: their eyes shine pale gold in her light and they never go fully dark.

fovWide.description: its field of view wide and close (degrees; the game's is 20).

aimWide.description: how far out (m) the middle of the view looks at its lowest (as she first looks: at the forest).

pan.description: degrees a second panning (left, right) and tilting wide, slower zoomed in (alike on screen).

zoomStep.description: a step of the zoom (the wheel, Z and X, the gamepad's shoulder buttons; 0 wide to 1 close).

bend.description: the world's bend inside it (the treetops' is camera.curve.treetop; gentler, so the far side stays in view).

reach.description: tree crowns are drawn out to this many metres (the island's far side; past the scenery's radius crowns alone).

thinFrom.description: past thinFrom metres only one crown in thin is drawn, thinGrow times as big (the cheaper far forest).

wedge.description: what's drawn is what lies within its view's width and this many degrees either side, listed again each half of it panned.

moonSpread.description: the game's moon stands at a bearing round north, the game's view this many degrees across.

consHold.description: tonight's constellation: its stars' brightness (1 the sky's brightest), its faint dotted lines' strength, fading in once she's held the view on it consHold seconds.

resolution.description: its picture's resolution (1 the game's pixels, 2 twice as fine, 0.5 twice as coarse; up to 3).

telescope.description: The telescope in the treehouse's crow's nest, which she can walk up to and look through full screen.

smoke.description: Smoke puffs rising from every fire (campfires, bonfires, torches, the charcoal burner) high into the sky before they fade.

clouds.description: The clouds drifting high over the forest, lit from below by the party's colours.

ground.description: the faint flash on the forest (0 none).

lightning.description: about every so many seconds a cloud in view flickers (flashes per strike), sometimes with a forked bolt toward the horizon.

sky.description: The night sky that shows over the bend in treetop mode (on; ?sky=off leaves the plain dark background there, which costs nothing): stars (how many, 0-1), moon (brightness).

phasePeriod.description: seconds from new moon to new moon.

phaseStart.description: its phase at the start (0 new, 0.25 first quarter, 0.5 full).

orbit.description: seconds to cross the sky once (it rises at the left from behind the far forest and sets at the right), from arcStart (0-1 of the way).

left.description: how far across the screen it goes.

low.description: the height of its way up the sky band (fractions of the screen from the bottom: low is behind the far forest).

tint.description: how much of its colour the moonlight on the world takes (0 none, 1 all).

bloodTint.description: the same for a red (blood) moon, a little more so it reads through the night grade (the rendering builder, #252).

disc.description: the sky moon's size, times its old one (1.5: a crescent survives the sky's tilt-shift blur, the art director, #252).

floor.description: the dancefloor's moon before the first wave: palette (dusky violet, slate blue, soft silver, 0-255), size (the moon's radius, a share of the floor's), stars (the share of the floor's sky twinkling round it), flare (seconds the full moon flares out into the party when the first wave comes).

moon.description: The moon in the sky, and the odd red, blue or gold moon that comes and goes during a run.

sigilSpill.description: Placed sigils glow like small lights in their creature's neon, tinting the grass, the ground and whoever stands near.

fireworks.description: The fireworks show over a soundsystem when a wave is celebrated.

combatLight.description: Her light shrinks while she explores a wild area and grows during a fight, so the fight is lit.

nightLight.description: How far her light reaches when the camera is far out, over the treetops and while she stargazes on the beach.

glowFalloff.description: how fast it falls off, as (1 - distance/(reach × glowNear))^glowFalloff.

glowNear.description: the share of that reach where her light has fallen to dark.

lightBudget.description: how many of the nearest point lights (campfires, magic stones, the dancefloor) light the scene at once.

find.description: tonight's find's own pale gold-white light (the finds style guide, docs/art-guide/FINDS.md: the brightest and whitest thing on its patch, brighter than her lantern; out once it's taken).

knee.description: Bright lights ease off toward a ceiling instead of burning to white, so lit ground keeps its texture.

lights.description: How far (reach, metres) and how strongly each kind of light lights its surroundings.

glowPower.description: How bright the witch's own glow is, brightest under her and fading smoothly to dark at its reach.

moonHue.description: (times tone.moon): a colder moon, a little stronger, so it rims what it lights.

hazeHue.description: (its brightness, 0 to 1): the fog the forest fades into, violet.

hazeNear.description: where the fog starts and is whole (metres from the witch; nearer than haze.near and haze.far, which still set how far scenery is drawn).

mist.description: the low ground mist's strength (instead of mist.strength).

glowHue.description: the witch's glow, warmer, so the party's lights are the warm ones in the wood.

grade.description: a grade over the finished picture, draining the dark and middle tones' colour (gradeDesat of it) toward a cold tint (hue and saturation), by grade, fading out up to gradePivot brightness, so the bright warm lights keep their colour.

partyWarm.description: the soundsystems' light, warm amber, pink and gold (one per variant, instead of their crystal cyan, violet and amber), wider and stronger.

decorLights.description: the party decor's lights (lanterns, campfires), how many an area lights (instead of partyObjects.lightsPerArea) and how far and strong, so each party is pools of warm light with dark between.

rimHue.description: A thin moonlit edge on the witch and every creature, so they stand out against the dark.

witchGlow.description: how much of her own glow lights the witch herself (0: none, as before), so she stands in her pool of light.

moonUpWrap.description: How evenly the moon's fill lights every face, so tree crowns don't light up as a lattice of dots.

styledRim.description: Extra rim and glow on the witch in the bold and reference art styles, where she would otherwise vanish in her own light.

areaEase.description: how fast the mood eases from one area's to the next (a second).

areas.description: Each kind of area's own fog colour, tint and mist (teal over bogs, violet in dead woods, pale mist on the moor and so on).

spooky.description: ambientHue and ambient (times the tuning's ambient): the shadows' colour and brightness, a deep blue-green.

light.description: The night lighting's overall mood: the spooky grade over the plain light, and the moon's fill on everything facing up.

lightSources.description: Light sources placed by seed, on a grid of spacing metres, mostly in clearings and at area edges: the chance per spot of a campfire, a magic stone, or a pond mirroring the moon (wetPond in wet areas: wetland, stream, bog, beaver pond, moor).

haze.description: the twilight haze fades the forest from near to far metres from the witch; nothing is drawn beyond far.

trees.description: a crown-sized shadow under every tree too, cast away from the moon.

tint.description: every shadow (scenery's, the trees' and palms', and the blobs under creatures, the witch, bushes and small things) at its darkest goes from black toward the complement of the light it lies in by tint (0: black): a campfire's orange throws blue-violet, plain moonlight a warm shade.

cast.description: Creatures, the witch, bushes and props darken where trunk and scenery shadows fall on them, not just the ground.

foot.description: How a trunk's shadow fades in at its foot, widens, fades as she comes close, and darkens the grass it falls on.

scenery.description: Scenery (ruins, rocks, relics, runestones, soundsystems) casts shadows from her glow and the fires too.

glowLight.description: a glowing caster's (a runestone, a soundsystem) toward a soft shade of its own colour by glowLight (0: as dark as any).

sceneryFoot.description: scenery's shadow, cast from its middle, fades in from nothing over its own half-width and sceneryFoot metres past it (0: none).

sceneryTaper.description: scenery's shadow is pinched to a third at its foot and opens to full over its half-width and sceneryTaper times its width past it (a wide ruin over more ground than a narrow runestone; at most 0.6 of its shadow's length; 0: none).

lightReach.description: how far a soundsystem's or a runestone's light throws the trees', props' and scenery's shadows, in metres (0: none), past its own glow's reach so the trees round its clearing catch it.

shadows.description: a small contact shadow under the witch, each bush, creature and prop; Ed's tuned values: strength 0.75, long 2.5, glowReach 50, glowHeight 1.25, soft, core 0.8, across 1, and lights.campfire.reach 40.

species.description: every species fights with its own attack in the grammar (config/species-attacks.json, by biome and island phase), its kind's own moves and its pack's turns as before; false (?attacks=old) the old ones.

attacks.description: The composable attacks (docs/plans/attack-grammar.md, src/rules/attacks/): reactionFloor, the least warning (s) any attack and each child it makes gives from its first telegraph to its first harm; one under it is lengthened to it, silently in the game, said so in the Fight Arena.

gpu.description: How much graphics memory the game lets itself use, letting go of the art used longest ago when it's over.

mist.description: A low mist drifting just above the ground.

soft.description: the front's soft edge (m either side), size: its rolling noise (m).

sea.description: The loading mist lies over the sea too and burns off last, once all the land is in.

loadingMist.description: A glowing mist over the parts of the island still loading, rolling back from the treehouse as their trees arrive.

strength.description: a band at its brightest (in the moon's hue, paled), added as light.

lightRings.description: Faint rings of moonlight across the treetops (now switched off), and the glory round her shadow on the leaves (off too).

size.description: the glyph (m across: under about 20 its one-pixel strokes are finer than the treetop view's pixels and it smears).

lift.description: how high its middle floats over the projector (m).

glyph.description: how bright (added light; past about 0.7 the bloom swallows its outline).

powerUp.description: the flicker as it comes on when the soundsystem has risen (s).

collapse.description: how long it takes to fold to a line and go out when the soundsystem is destroyed (s).

turn.description: how far it turns either way (degrees).

fadeFar.description: How far from her a soundsystem's hologram fades out; a damaged soundsystem's hologram glitches.

holograms.description: Each soundsystem projects a turning hologram of its area's animal sigil into the sky above the trees.

watching.description: Leafy plants near her path lean toward where she just was, as if the trees are watching her.

moonbeams.description: How strong the diagonal moonbeam bands are, times the style's Moonbeams knob: 0 is off (Ed, v108: they read as stripes over a dense canopy).

enragedTint.description: An enraged creature's whole sprite is tinted toward a colour, keeping its shading.

anger.description: A pixel 💢 popping beside an enraged creature's head.

partyGlow.description: every happy and leashed animal has sparkles twinkling pixels round it, each lit for a moment about rate times a second, size times three game pixels, at strength brightness (additive); leashed ones keep their collar on top.

looks.description: How creatures look in their different states, such as the angry brows of an enraged one.

tone.description: Contrast: ambient scales the twilight fill (lower is darker shade under the canopy), moon the moonlight (both lowered for Ed's dark forest, v149); black is the black point and gamma the curve applied to the whole picture, so dark goes near-black and lit stays bright.

bloom.description: a gentle glow round bright things (strength 0 or on false turns it off; threshold: how bright a pixel must be to glow).

skyBlur.description: the share of the blur the night sky takes: 1 blurs it as the ground, 0 leaves its stars sharp; a slider in the decisions panel, with the treetops' strength.

stackSharp.description: her sigil stack over her hat kept out of the blur, sharp at any height, however tall; false blurs it with the rest.

strength.description: the blur at the screen's edges, in pixels.

band.description: the height of the sharp band (0-1 of the screen).

centre.description: where it sits (0 top, 0.5 middle, 1 bottom).

treetop.description: A stronger miniature-world blur when she's up in the treetops.

tiltShift.description: blurs the top and bottom of the screen so the forest looks like a miniature.
